from.place: compare Koszul Hom complexes with alternating Cech complex

title: Koszul Hom colimit is the alternating Cech complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$, and let $M^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For each $e\ge1$ let $K_\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ be the Koszul chain complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], with differential $d_n:K_n\to K_{n-1}$, and for $1\le i_0<\cdots<i_p\le r$ write $[i_0,\ldots,i_p]=e_{i_0}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_p}$ for the corresponding basis vector of $K_{p+1}$, so that $d_{p+2}([i_0,\ldots,i_{p+1}])=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^jf_{i_j}^e[i_0,\ldots,\widehat{i_j},\ldots,i_{p+1}]$. Define the shifted negative cochain complex $I^\bullet=I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ by $I^i=K_{1-i}(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ for $i\le0$, $I^i=0$ for $i>0$, with differential $d_I^i=-d_{1-i}:I^i\to I^{i+1}$ for $i<0$ and $d_I^i=0$ for $i\ge0$. The transition $I^\bullet(f_1^{e+1},\ldots,f_r^{e+1})\to I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$ is the map of complexes sending $[i_0,\ldots,i_p]$ to $f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}[i_0,\ldots,i_p]$; precomposition with it makes $e\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e),M^\bullet)$ a directed system of Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex] (taken for $A$-modules, i.e. on the one-point site), whose degree-$n$ term is $\prod_{p}\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^{-p},M^{n+p})$; call $\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^{-p},M^q)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(K_{p+1},M^q)$ its bidegree $(p,q)$ part. Let $T^\bullet$ be the total complex of the alternating (ordered) Cech double complex of $M^\bullet$ for $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ (the module form of the alternating Cech complex of [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes] for the covering of $D(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(f_r)$ by the $D(f_i)$): its bidegree $(p,q)$ part is $C^{p,q}=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}M^q_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}$ for $p\ge0$ (zero for $p<0$), $T^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}C^{p,q}$, and for $s\in C^{p,q}$ the differential is $d_T(s)=\delta(s)+(-1)^pd_M(s)$, where $\delta(s)_{i_0\ldots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j\,s_{i_0\ldots\widehat{i_j}\ldots i_{p+1}}$ (each term mapped into $M^q_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_{p+1}}}$ by the localization map) and $d_M$ acts entrywise. Then the map $\Phi:\varinjlim_e\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e),M^\bullet)\to T^\bullet$ which on bidegree $(p,q)$ is the fraction map $t\mapsto\big(t([i_0,\ldots,i_p])/(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p})^e\big)_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}$ multiplied by $(-1)^{pq+p(p-1)/2}$ is well defined and is an isomorphism of complexes of $A$-modules; in particular it is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: The transition is a map of complexes: for $J=\{i_0<\cdots<i_{p+1}\}$ and $f_J=f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_{p+1}}$, applying $d_{p+2}$ at exponent $e$ to $f_J[J]$ gives $\sum_j(-1)^jf_J f_{i_j}^e[J\setminus i_j]=\sum_j(-1)^jf_{i_j}^{e+1}f_{J\setminus i_j}[J\setminus i_j]$, which is the transition applied to $d_{p+2}[J]$ at exponent $e+1$. For $t\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(K_{p+1},M^q)$ at exponent $e$ define the unsigned fraction map $\psi(t)_{i_0\ldots i_p}=t([i_0,\ldots,i_p])/(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p})^e$ on the Koszul basis [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. The transition sends $t$ to $t'$ with $t'([J])=f_Jt([J])$, and $f_Jt([J])/f_J^{e+1}=t([J])/f_J^e$, so $\psi$ is compatible with the transitions and descends to the filtered colimit (elementary).

In each total degree $n$ only $0\le p\le r-1$ contribute, so $\operatorname{Hom}^n$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is a finite product, and filtered colimits of $A$-modules commute with finite products (elementary). Since $K_{p+1}$ is free with basis the $[i_0,\ldots,i_p]$, $i_0<\cdots<i_p$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], $t\mapsto(t([J]))_J$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(K_{p+1},M^q)$ with $\prod_JM^q$ (universal property of a free module, elementary), and under this identification the transition is multiplication by $f_J$ in the $J$-entry. By [lem-sc-module-localization-filtered-colimit] applied to $f=f_J$ (indexing from $e=1$ is cofinal), the colimit of $M^q\xrightarrow{f_J}M^q\to\cdots$ maps isomorphically to $M^q_{f_J}$ by $m\mapsto m/f_J^e$ at stage $e$. Hence $\psi$ is an isomorphism $\varinjlim_e\operatorname{Hom}_A(K_{p+1},M^q)\to C^{p,q}=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}M^q_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}$, the bidegree $(p,q)$ term of the alternating Cech complex of the statement [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes].

Let $t\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(K_{p+1},M^q)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(I^{-p},M^q)$, of total degree $n=p+q$. By [def-pur-hom-complex], $d(t)=d_M\circ t-(-1)^n t\circ d_I^{-p-1}$, and $d_I^{-p-1}=-d_{p+2}$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], so $d(t)=d_M\circ t+(-1)^{p+q}\,t\circ d_{p+2}$, with $d_M\circ t$ in bidegree $(p,q+1)$ and $t\circ d_{p+2}$ in bidegree $(p+1,q)$. Clearly $\psi(d_M\circ t)=d_M\psi(t)$. For $J=\{i_0<\cdots<i_{p+1}\}$, $\psi(t\circ d_{p+2})_J=\sum_j(-1)^jf_{i_j}^et([J\setminus i_j])/f_J^e=\sum_j(-1)^jt([J\setminus i_j])/f_{J\setminus i_j}^e=\delta(\psi t)_J$, with $\delta$ the alternating face differential of the statement [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes]. So $\psi(d t)=d_M\psi t+(-1)^{p+q}\delta\psi t$, while $d_T=\delta+(-1)^pd_M$ on $C^{p,q}$. Hence $\Phi=\epsilon_{p,q}\psi$ is a map of complexes iff $\epsilon_{p,q+1}=(-1)^p\epsilon_{p,q}$ and $(-1)^{p+q}\epsilon_{p+1,q}=\epsilon_{p,q}$. For $\epsilon_{p,q}=(-1)^{pq+p(p-1)/2}$: $\epsilon_{p,q+1}/\epsilon_{p,q}=(-1)^p$ and $\epsilon_{p+1,q}/\epsilon_{p,q}=(-1)^{q+(p+1)p/2-p(p-1)/2}=(-1)^{p+q}$, as required. Check $r=2$, $M$ in degree $0$, $t:K_1\to M^0$: $d(t)=t\circ d_2$, $d(t)(e_1\wedge e_2)=f_1^et(e_2)-f_2^et(e_1)$, so $\Phi(dt)_{12}=t(e_2)/f_2^e-t(e_1)/f_1^e=\delta(\Phi t)_{12}$ ($\epsilon_{0,0}=\epsilon_{1,0}=1$). By Step 2, $\Phi$ is bijective in each bidegree, hence an isomorphism of complexes.
An isomorphism of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism. For $r=0$ both sides are zero; for $r=1$ both sides are $M^\bullet_{f_1}$ with $\epsilon_{0,q}=1$.

tool_uses.why: The item needs the established identification of full ordered Cech cochains with the strictly increasing alternating rows; this generic Cech tool is not supplied by the Koszul duality unit.
